dedupe_keys.name: pypsa usa open source energy system optimisation model for the united states

description: PyPSA-USA is an open-source model of the bulk transmission system of the United States, built as a configurable workflow on the PyPSA framework. It is developed by the PyPSA-USA authors, including Kamran Tehranchi, Trevor Barnes and Martha Frysztacki, with contact through Stanford University, and draws on the design of PyPSA-Eur so that US studies can use the same open tool chain. The workflow builds a power system model that can be used for capacity expansion planning, production cost simulation and power flow analysis, with documentation on ReadTheDocs covering installation, usage and contribution. Coverage is the US bulk power system. The code is accessible on GitHub under the MIT licence at no cost, with a first Zenodo release (version 0.0.1) and later tags up to version 0.9, and the latest commit in August 2026. Caveats: the README gives few details of data sources and the pre-1.0 version signals ongoing change, so users should read the documentation for assumptions. Simulation uses are US capacity expansion, dispatch and transmission studies. Related records: model-pypsa-eur is the model it follows, and model-pypsa is the underlying framework.
